packageRules.description: CI gates every PR (nextest, vitest, playwright, clippy, cargo-deny), so anything below a major merges itself once green.
Refreshing the lockfiles is how transitive advisories reach us — a direct dependency bump cannot pull a patched sub-dependency on its own.

The Rust version is pinned in three places (rust-toolchain.toml, the dtolnay/rust-toolchain action, and the Dockerfile's rust image) and they must move together. Never automerged: a new toolchain relints and reformats the workspace, which is a deliberate change.

pnpm is pinned in web/package.json, e2e/package.json and the pnpm/action-setup input. web/pnpm-workspace.yaml documents that these are one atomic change — pnpm 9 hard-fails on the workspace file this repo now ships.
Node is pinned in the Dockerfile's web-builder stage and in actions/setup-node; keep the build and CI on the same major.

web/pnpm-workspace.yaml pins these EXACTLY, to deduplicate the ProseMirror core that @tiptap/pm and y-prosemirror both depend on: when pnpm resolves them to different patches, tsc fails with a wall of 'not assignable' errors between two structurally identical Node types. That is the whole reason. Surfaced on the dashboard rather than automerged because a bump has to be checked for re-duplication, not because any version is suspect.

Security floors in web/pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides. Raising them is welcome, but they exist because a parent hard-pins a vulnerable version, so a bump here needs a human to confirm the parent still resolves.
Playwright ships its browser binaries per version; a bump changes what the e2e suite actually runs against.
